text:
Luca (CSM): FYI Pelagic hit an onboarding snag this morning 10% of sessions show tail latency >2s during midday surge. Renewal chatter in two months so want to be proactive. Thinking compact-int4 trial + adaptive routing with short-term batching. Thoughts?

Priya (Solutions Eng): Can we quantify expected quality delta? Pelagic uses a lot of short prompts but high request rate. If quality stable, int4 looks promising. Also: client uses eu-west primarily, maybe route overflow to eu-central.

Derek (ML Eng): We ran internal sims on their anonymized prompts: compact-chat-v1-int4 shows median latency -40% and cost -50%, quality delta measured on ROUGE-like metric ~0.8% (within tolerance per contract). Suggest a 5% canary then 25% if good. Add adaptive batching for 100-200ms window to smooth tail.

Anya (SRE): I can add an overflow route to eu-central and create a dynamic batcher for their service id. Need to bump request concurrency limit by +15% for the test. I'll file infra ticket and add monitoring.

Luca (CSM): Great. I'll book a 30m customer call tomorrow to explain the safety nets. Priya can you prepare a short one-page note including rollback criteria and expected unit savings?

Priya (Solutions Eng): Yep. Draft below (will send via email):
- Objective: reduce p95/p99 latency and per-token cost without noticeable quality regression.
- Plan: 5% canary -> 25% -> 60% over 20m intervals. Auto rollback on >3% quality regression OR >25% p99 increase.
- Safety: route overflow to eu-central, enable short prefix cache (30s) for repeated system messages, turn on ephemeral batching 100ms.

Derek (ML Eng): Rollout snippet: 
```yaml
canary:
  steps: [5,25,60]
  interval_seconds: 1200
rollback:
  quality_threshold_pct: 3
  p99_threshold_pct: 25
routing:
  primary: eu-west-1
  overflow: eu-central-1
  overflow_percent: 20
model:
  canary: compact-chat-v1-int4
  fallback: compact-chat-v1-fp16
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_delay_ms: 100
prefix_cache:
  enabled: true
  ttl_s: 30
```

Anya (SRE): Ops tickets created: #OPS-8135 (overflow route), #OPS-8136 (concurrency bump), #OPS-8137 (batcher). I'll attach dashboards and alert rules: p99>1.6s, quality-drop>2%.

OpsBot: rollout-plan-4971234567 created, canary-route deployed -> canary-4971234567-pelagic-1 (status: active) :white_check_mark:

Luca (CSM): I'll include the expected cost delta (-~48% per token) and the renewal note. Priya please make the exec note customer-facing friendly.

Priya (Solutions Eng): Will do. Also attaching a short A/B prompt set (5 examples) for Pelagic to sanity-check outputs during the canary.

Derek (ML Eng): One more: enable a short-lived quality monitor that runs the A/B set every 5 minutes and posts a slip if average score drops >1.5%.

Anya (SRE): Alert hook added. If canary trips we'll rollback to fallback model and drain overflow.

Luca (CSM): Thanks team. Will follow up after the 10am test and update the account health doc with results and next steps.
